correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé equivalence of adjacency-only rook graphs R_{a,b}=K_a□K_b for every q>=1. If both factor sizes agree after q-truncation up to swap, Duplicator prolongs separate partial bijections on row/column coordinate values through all q moves, preserving equality and edge relation. Conversely rank2 existence of a nonedge distinguishes 2D factors from complete cases; for rank s>=3, s-clique existence detects max(a,b)>=s, while universal requirement of s−2 common neighbors for every edge detects min(a,b)>=s. Complete cases are counted by existence of distinct vertices, handling q=1,2 explicitly. Therefore exact q-type count is q(q+1)/2 and largest least rook-family representative is q². Independent recursive EF game checks passed 55 graph pairs at q=1 and q=2 and 21 pairs at q=3; the all-q proof is symbolic.
residual_risks: The universal common-neighbor formula is rank s including its two outer universal quantifiers and s−2 existentials, not rank s−2.
Only family-relative least representatives, no arbitrary-graph minimization.

value.rationale: Rook graphs are a canonical family of finite 2-factor Hamming graphs and line graphs of K_{a,b}. The adjacency language hides the coordinate sorts; exact recoverable dimensions at each FO quantifier rank, type count q(q+1)/2, and sharp least-representative order q² give a complete family-specific logical-complexity invariant, not an arbitrary finite example.

limitations: FO adjacency/equality language only, no named coordinates or counting quantifiers; within rook family only.
